newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: SIA unable to hedge jet fuel much 2nd hf.
newsitem.headline: SIA unable to hedge jet fuel much 2nd hf.

text.p: Singapore Airlines Ltd (SIA), which traditionally hedges some of its jet fuel requirements, has not been able to hedge much for the second half of the year, said SIA deputy chairman and chief executive officer (CEO) Cheong Choong Kong.

In an interview with Reuters on Wednesday, Cheong said that for the first half of the company's financial year ending September 30, 1996, the airline saved Singapore $20 million through its hedging activities.

"But in the second half, we have not been able to hedge very much. All the experts were predicting fuel prices to come down in the second half. There were also expectations of Iraqi oil entering the market...but then things did not turn out," Cheong said.

"Then airlines started rushing in to try and lock in future prices which even exacerbated the situation. We have not been able to hedge -- it was too costly. Fuel prices were rising too fast," he said.
Singapore jet fuel prices are currently around US$30.50 per barrel, up more than 30 percent year-on-year.
Cheong said the outlook for jet fuel prices looked uncertain and would depend on the severity of the winter in Europe and North America.
